card.name: Tango
card.tagline: Iconic Río de la Plata partner dance and global musical genre.
card.profile: Tango is a partner and social dance and musical genre that originated in the 1880s in the impoverished port neighborhoods along the Río de la Plata (Buenos Aires and Montevideo), born from Argentine milonga, Spanish-Cuban habanera, and Uruguayan candombe. It encompasses a family of related dances (tango, vals, milonga) and styles ranging from close-embrace milonguero to open salon and stage tango (English Wikipedia). The bandoneón is its signature instrument.
card.insight: Tango is the most recognizable embodiment of Río de la Plata identity and the only fully UNESCO-inscribed dance in this region's catalog (2009); it both embodies and encourages diversity and cultural dialogue (UNESCO; English Wikipedia).

lessons.title: Beginner Argentine Tango Basics

parts.note: The teachers introduce themselves and the topic.
The teachers explain the neutral position and weight transfer.
The teachers break down the side step.
The teachers break down the forward and back steps.
The teachers combine the side, forward, and back steps.
The teachers introduce the box step (baldosas).
The teachers explain how to listen to the music and practice the box step with music.
The teachers demonstrate the box step with a partner.

steps.name: side step
steps.description: A lateral step followed by closing the feet.

steps.name: forward step
steps.description: A step forward followed by closing the feet.

steps.name: back step
steps.description: A step backward followed by closing the feet.

steps.name: box step (baldosas)
steps.description: A combination of side, forward, and back steps.

lessons.teacher_style: The teachers work as a pair, with one demonstrating and explaining while the other models the partner's role. They maintain a friendly, encouraging tone throughout the lesson.
lessons.distinctive_method: The teachers use Spanish terminology for the steps, which adds authenticity to the lesson.
what_works: The teachers break down the steps into small, manageable parts.
The use of a partner helps to visualize the steps.
what_hinders: The video is a bit repetitive.

evidence.observation: The teachers stand side-by-side, facing the camera, introducing the lesson.
The teachers demonstrate the neutral position with feet together and toes slightly turned out.
The teachers demonstrate the side step by sliding one foot to the side and then closing it.
The teachers demonstrate the forward step by stepping forward and then closing the feet.
The teachers demonstrate the box step by combining the side, forward, and back steps.
